subject: Best way to evaluate test information (or interpret a & b parameters) for models with 3 or more dimensions

messages.author: 595f772c619c0cb0
messages.subject: Best way to evaluate test information (or interpret a & b parameters) for models with 3 or more dimensions
parts:
Dear Dr. Chalmers,

          I'm a researcher working on item analysis and proposed shortening of several interest rating scales. Normally for unidimensional models, I would plot 2 test information curves with and without the item(s) with low discrimination parameter to show that the test information does not suffer by the removal of those items. For IRT models with 3 or more dimensions, I am not sure of the best way to evaluate results in a similar way. Thanks to mirt, I am able to use MHRM with the gpcm to get a1, a2, a3 (...) parameters and the d1 to d4 (5-point rating scale) parameters and point out items with the lowest a-values. Is there a good way to interpret or present these results?

Many Thanks.

Sincerely,
Colin Wee Jian Ming
Doctoral Student
Industrial-Organizational Psychology
University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Best way to evaluate test information (or interpret a & b parameters) for models with 3 or more dimensions
parts:
Plots for 3+ dimensions are much more difficult to work with, so you don't really get the nice unidimensional outputs. Plus, the multidimenisonal models are compensatory in nature, so if you have cross-loading you have to interpret all the results as partial coefficients. You can try to get some plots out of the plot() function (see the documentation for what limited support is offered for 3 dimensional models), but overall it's usually better to interpret the coefficients directly. HTH.

Phil

Dear Dr. Chalmers,

         Thank you for the reply. Sorry to trouble you with one more question, regarding errors resulting from my most complex dimensional model. For a rating scale (1-5) studying interest in influencing others, I have 8 related subscales (Management, business, marketing, etc) with 4 items each. 

          My script, which had been working with all other models with fewer dimensions, halted on the first iteration with an error that I suspect may be caused by the addition of an 8th subscale to the model (error listed below). I tried to remove any of the 8 subscales from the model to make 7-dimensions and the model converged without errors or warnings. I also tried changing the starting seed but to no avail. I wonder if you have any input on the cause of this---are 8 dimensional models just not possible, or is my script faulty, and is there a workaround? 

Thank you so much for your time, I'm trying to craft a dissertation proposal on the application of IRT to interest items, if I get to the next stage I'll be sure to credit you for your help and your super handy mirt package!  

Sincerely,
Colin Wee

##Model##

> gpcm_modI <- '
Mgmt = 1, 2, 3, 4
Bus = 5, 6, 7, 8
Mkt = 9, 10, 11, 12
PA = 13, 14, 15, 16
PS = 17, 18, 19, 20
Sal = 21, 22, 23, 24
Pol = 25, 26, 27, 28
Law = 29, 30, 31, 32
COV = Mgmt*Bus*Mkt*PA*PS*Sal*Pol*Law 
'

##script##

gpcm_fitI <- mirt(data, gpcm_modI, method = "MHRM", itemtype = 'gpcm', technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000))


##error message##

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Best way to evaluate test information (or interpret a & b parameters) for models with 3 or more dimensions
parts:
These types of errors occasionally occur due to poor starting values. You may want to try the GenRandomPars input to mirt() to generate a random set of starting values. Alternatively, and probably much better, you could try to give more helpful starting parameters based on previously estimated models, or by first constraining all the factors to be uncorrelated and then use these estimated item parameters in the subsequent estimation of the correlated model (I would personally start with this approach as random starting value generation is really a last resort). HTH.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Best way to evaluate test information (or interpret a & b parameters) for models with 3 or more dimensions
parts:
Dear Dr, Chalmers,

          Awesome, using the uncorrelated model to estimate values then using 'pars = values' for the corrected model worked without errors or warnings. Thanks so much! My script is below in case I'm making a mistake somewhere (first time using the pars argument).

#getting the values data frame, gpcm_modI is the model without covariances#
values <- mirt(data, gpcm_modI, pars = 'values', method = "MHRM", itemtype = 'gpcm', technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000))

#running gpcm_modI2, the model with covariances#
gpcm_fitI2 <- mirt(data, gpcm_modI2, pars = values, method = "MHRM", itemtype = 'gpcm', technical = list(NCYCLES = 2000))

Thanks once again!

Sincerely,
Colin Wee
